title: IRIS: A 8.55 mJ/frame Spatial Computing SoC for Real-time Interactable-Rendering and Surface-aware-Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: Real-time spatial computing with 3D Gaussian Splatting requires specialized hardware for low-latency, energy-efficient rendering and surface modeling.
method: IRIS is a domain-specific SoC optimized for 3D Gaussian Splatting with dedicated pipelines for Gaussian rasterization, differentiable rendering, and surface reconstruction, achieving energy efficiency through algorithmic optimization.

title: Seeking Cost-Optimal Infrastructure Size for Distributed Filesystems: A Ceph Case Study
problem: Predicting distributed filesystem I/O performance based solely on hardware configuration is not straightforward
method: Empirical evaluation of Ceph DFS varying CPU cores, RAM, and disk bandwidth using Linux hotplug and Cgroups

title: 3.3 A Passive Switched-Capacitor-Based Multimode Amplifier with a Logarithmic Conformity Error of 0.75% from -25 to 200°C
problem: Harsh geothermal and high-temperature environments (up to 200°C) require sensor front-end amplifiers with wide dynamic range (>80dB), low temperature drift, and accurate phase/amplitude across extreme temperature spans. Existing logarithmic amplifiers exhibit high temperature dependence; low-drift amplifiers require complex trimming and compensation.
method: A passive switched-capacitor (SC) topology with multimode operation achieves high dynamic range and temperature stability. The design leverages discrete-time SC amplification to improve noise efficiency while avoiding the thermal drift issues of traditional logarithmic or low-drift amplifiers, using novel compensation mechanisms for stability across -25 to 200°C.

title: LUT-DLA: Lookup Table as Efficient Extreme Low-Bit Deep Learning Accelerator
problem: Scalar quantization cannot reduce DNN bit-width below 1-bit, capping compression gains; existing accelerators lack hardware support for vector-quantization-based LUT approaches that could push beyond this limit.
method: LUT-DLA converts DNN weight tensors into lookup tables via vector quantization, replacing multiply-accumulate operations with LUT index lookups and accumulations. The LUTBoost algorithm trains DNNs through a multistage process to learn LUT-compatible vector codebooks. A co-design space exploration framework evaluates the trade-off between LUT table size, codebook dimensionality, model accuracy, and hardware cost to select optimal hardware configurations. The ASIC accelerator implements LUT fetch-and-accumulate dataflow units that directly consume quantized indices to perform inference.

title: PIMoE: Towards Efficient MoE Transformer Deployment on NPU-PIM System through Throttle-Aware Task Offloading
problem: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformer inference suffers from data transfer overhead and imbalanced workload distribution between NPU and processing-in-memory (PIM) components.
method: PIMoE combines NPU and PIM in a heterogeneous system with throttle-aware task offloading to balance workload based on processing capability, and designs a near-memory-controller data condenser to handle sparse data layout translation between NPU and PIM domains.

title: 24.5 A 72GS/s 9b Time-Interleaved Pipeline-SAR ADC Achieving 55.3/49.3dB SFDR at 20GHz/Nyquist Inputs in 16nm FinFET
problem: Time-interleaved (TI) ADCs for optical receivers (>100Gb/s) require near-100GS/s sampling with high SFDR (>55dB) at wideband (>20GHz) inputs. Massive TI factors degrade SFDR due to bandwidth mismatch and implicit distortion in the interleaver; sampling-capacitor tuning addresses only first-order correction; high-frequency input buffers introduce distortion and gain attenuation.
method: A 72GS/s 9b time-interleaved pipeline-SAR ADC employs linearized wideband input buffers, dual-path bootstrapped switches (BS), and R/R-based open-loop amplifier to minimize inter-stage gain (ISG) calibration complexity. The pipeline-SAR architecture combines pipeline linearity with SAR efficiency at 1.125GS/s per unit, scaled to 72GS/s via 64-fold time interleaving.

title: Uno: A One-Stop Solution for Inter- and Intra-Data Center Congestion Control and Reliable Connectivity
problem: Cloud/AI workloads generate heterogeneous traffic (intra-DC and inter-DC) with different RTT characteristics. Existing congestion control treats them separately, causing rate unfairness and slow loss recovery. Need unified solution.
method: Uno unified system combining: (1) Transport protocol for rapid congestion reaction and fair rate control; (2) Load balancing with erasure coding and adaptive routing. Single control mechanism handles both traffic types.

title: Pave: Information Flow Control for Privacy-preserving Online Data Processing Services
problem: When users submit personal data to remote online services for processing, they have no technical guarantee that the service will not leak their data, because the processing logic runs in an untrusted server environment entirely outside the user's control.
method: Pave provides a sandboxed execution environment (PaveBox) for arbitrary data-processing programs on a remote server. PaveBox, built on Intel SGX (a hardware trusted execution environment), intercepts all data flows into and out of the sandbox using a runtime monitor that applies information flow control (IFC) policies. Allowed flows are permitted without interference to preserve program functionality; disallowed flows (those that would expose user data) are blocked. Users can verify PaveBox's integrity and confidentiality via SGX remote attestation. The system's security is formalized in a model and proved, with quantitative analysis via prototype experiments.

title: An Energy-Efficient High-Utilization Hardware Architecture for Attention Mechanism in Transformer using Balanced Systolic Array and Multi-Row Interleaved Operation Ordering
problem: Existing attention accelerators use conventional systolic arrays that cannot balance data reuse, register savings, and utilization; layer-by-layer scheduling causes high SRAM energy for intermediate results.
method: Two-pronged architecture: (1) Balanced Systolic Array (BSA) redesigns tiling to improve data reuse and utilization to 99.5% vs conventional SAs, (2) Multi-Row Interleaved operation ordering groups multiple rows to reduce intermediate data writes to SRAM by 31.7%.

title: CIPHERMATCH: Accelerating Homomorphic Encryption-Based String Matching via Memory-Efficient Data Packing and In-Flash Processing
problem: Homomorphic encryption (HE)-based exact string matching incurs prohibitive computational latency due to expensive HE operations (multiplication, rotation) and severe data movement overhead from the large ciphertext memory footprint. Prior HE string matching algorithms cannot efficiently handle these combined bottlenecks.
method: CIPHERMATCH is an algorithm-hardware co-design that (1) applies an optimized software-based data packing scheme to reduce ciphertext memory footprint, (2) reformulates the string matching algorithm to eliminate costly HE multiplications and rotations, replacing them with cheaper addition-only operations, and (3) introduces a new in-flash processing (IFP) architecture that performs computation near the flash storage to minimize data movement between memory and processor.

title: VSpGEMM: Exploiting Versal ACAP for High-Performance SpGEMM Acceleration
problem: Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is fundamental in deep learning and scientific computing, but sparse matrices require compact storage and produce irregular memory access patterns, creating communication and computation bottlenecks. Existing accelerators struggle with storage format overhead and intermediate product merging.
method: VSpGEMM is a hardware accelerator on Xilinx Versal ACAP exploiting AI Engines (AIEs) and programmable logic (PL). Introduces BCSX (block-wise compressed storage format) enabling fixed-pattern memory access for both row-major and column-major data. Employs multi-level tiling decomposing SpGEMM into hierarchical granularities fitting AIEs. Uses hybrid AIE/PL partitioning to orchestrate intermediate product merging, reducing memory utilization and communication demand.

title: An SRAM-Based Multi-Operand Architecture Implementing Multi-Bit Boolean Functions Using in-Memory Periphery Computing
problem: Conventional SRAM designs use same bitlines for read and write, limiting ability to implement complex Boolean operations in-memory. Multi-operand and arbitrary Boolean function support in SRAM peripheral logic requires new architectures.
method: Modified 9T SRAM cell with dedicated read lines separating read/write paths. Periphery circuitry implements M-operand N-bit Boolean operations via compute blocks with equality checkers and product lines using DeMorgan's theorem.

title: A 0.024mm2 All-Digital Fractional Output Divider with 257fs Worst-Case Jitter Using Split-DTC-Based Background Calibration
problem: Fractional output dividers (FODs) using digital-to-time converters (DTCs) suffer from PVT variations, gain errors, and integral nonlinearity (INL), degrading jitter performance significantly. Prior calibration methods require additional reference clocks or auxiliary PLLs, increasing area and complexity.
method: All-digital FOD using split-DTC-based background calibration measuring and correcting both DTC gain and INL errors without requiring reference clock or auxiliary PLL. Split DTCs enable self-referential gain and INL calibration.

title: 7.5 A 353mW 112Gb/s Discrete Multitone Wireline Receiver Datapath with Time-Based ADC in 5nm FinFET
problem: High-speed >100Gb/s wireline receivers using traditional PAM-4 designs with large feed-forward equalizers (FFE) and decision-feedback equalizers (DFE) face exponentially increasing complexity as ISI cursors grow, and struggle with channel ripples/notches.
method: A discrete multitone (DMT) receiver uses time-based ADC to convert analog signals, then applies per-tone equalization and MLSE to handle complex channels; DMT avoids the large FFE tap counts and DFE timing constraints of PAM-4.

title: Accelerating Number Theoretic Transform with Multi-GPU Systems for Efficient Zero Knowledge Proof
problem: Number Theoretic Transform (NTT), a key bottleneck in zero-knowledge proof generation, has not been efficiently parallelized across multiple GPUs because its butterfly permutation access pattern generates high inter-GPU communication overhead that offsets the compute gains from additional GPUs.
method: The paper redesigns the NTT algorithm for multi-GPU execution by restructuring the butterfly computation stages to localize data access within GPU memory and minimize the frequency and volume of inter-GPU data transfers. The approach introduces a GPU-topology-aware permutation schedule that maps NTT stages to GPU assignments so that communication-intensive permutation steps are batched and overlap-optimized with computation. NVLink or PCIe interconnect topology is leveraged to select inter-GPU transfer paths that maximize aggregate bandwidth.

title: 4.6 A 0.8V, 31ppm/°C, -40dB DC-to-GHz Power-Supply-Rejection Standard-Vth Core-MOS-Only Voltage Reference with a 294µm2Area
problem: PVT-independent voltage references at sub-1V core-supply operation face headroom limitations from BJT V_EB and current-source saturation voltage; existing approaches require DNW base structures (non-standard CMOS) or switching-mode ripple filters (large area).
method: A standard-Vth core-MOS-only voltage reference operating at 0.8V uses charge-pump or switched-capacitor techniques to reduce supply headroom requirements beyond traditional BJT approaches. Achieves 31ppm/°C temperature coefficient with -40dB power-supply-rejection ratio (PSRR) across DC-to-GHz frequencies. Compact design uses only core devices without DNW structures.
